summary: Quick company all-hands covering Q2 performance, product GA for Private deployment, Dedicated autoscaling plans, hiring updates, and roadmap priorities. Leadership emphasized production reliability, revenue growth in Dedicated, and next steps for docs and customer comms.
transcript:
Header: 2025-08-12 10:00 AM PDT - Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jane Park (CEO), Alex Chen (CTO), Lena Ortiz (VP Eng), Samir Patel (Head of Product), Maya Rao (Head of DevEx) + All Employees

Summary: Jane opens, Samir goes through Q2 metrics, Alex covers infra + Dedicated autoscaling, Lena covers hiring/eng org, Maya closes with docs and next steps. Q&A at end.

00:00 Jane Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time, uh, morning or afternoon depending where you are, um we're gonna kick off, real quick agenda: Q2 results, product updates, hiring, and a short q a at the end.
00:28 Jane Park: quick shout out to the ops team - we had a pretty big migration last month and latency SLo's held, so really appreciate y'all.
00:44 Audience: applause (muted)
00:52 Samir Patel: alright i'll jump into the numbers - Q2 ARR growth was 22% quarter over quarter, net new ARR from dedicated contracts was up 35%. small caveat: a chunk of expansion came from two mid-market customers moving to dedicated pools.
01:10 Samir Patel: gross margin improved slightly, we saw per-token costs drop via batching and cache improvements we shipped in june, so unit economics look better, but we still have work on tail-latency.
01:33 Alex Chen: yeah on tail latency - the runtime team rolled out a new KV caching heuristic; it cuts out about 20% p99 on long-history chats but there's some edge cases where kv warms are slow, we're iterating.
01:49 Jane Park: can you un-sugar that a bit alex? how worried should product teams be?
01:54 Alex Chen: not a big worry, it's targeted scenarios - think very long context and sequence-heavy workloads. for standard chat flows p95/p99 are stable. we also have autoscaling improvements planned for Dedicated.
02:12 Samir Patel: dedicated autoscaling is top ask from customers who need guaranteed throughput but also want cost efficiency; the plan is conservative canary then wider rollout.
02:25 Lena Ortiz: on infra staffing - we've added four inference infra engineers this quarter, two more joining next month. hiring velocity is up but ramp times are long.
02:40 Audience Member: quick q: what's the GA timeline for Private (vpc/on-prem)?
02:45 Samir Patel: good question - Private is GA next week, official docs and compliance checklist go live, we have a handful of initial customers in pilot, so this is a big milestone.
03:01 Maya Rao: docs will include deployment runbooks, KMS integration notes, and SOC2/ISO checklist. we'll also publish an FAQ for the partner channel.
03:17 Jane Park: huge - that's one of the thesis inflection points: Private gives us the enterprise seat at the table. make sure sales has the right one-pager.
03:29 Samir Patel: we'll circulate a short sales play deck, and a tech checklist for solutions engineers.
03:39 Alex Chen: technical note - Private uses the same runtime but with customers' VPC, we do not ship kv or telemetry to our hosted control plane unless authorized; encryption at rest is mandatory and we support customer KMS/HSM. small nuance in the transcript here: sometimes docs call it KMS-H-S-M, so we'll standardize.
04:05 Jane Park: ok let's move to product roadmap highlights. samir?
04:11 Samir Patel: roadmap: 1) Redwood Optimize beta - focused on batching, quantization recs by workload, 2) Dedicated autoscale and burst policies, 3) Embedding reranking performance improvements.
04:27 Samir Patel: Optimize will give automated suggestions - e g: for retrieval-heavy workloads we'll recommend higher batching and specific quantization profiles. it's not a magic button, it's guidance plus metrics.
04:41 Audience Member: will Optimize change model quality?
04:45 Samir Patel: no, the system suggests profiles and provides sim score delta estimates; changes are opt-in, and you can do A/B evals via the console.
04:57 Lena Ortiz: ops note - rolling out the canary means we'll need on-call support windows for three weeks, folks from infra/serving will get invites.
05:10 Jane Park: hiring/org - people ops is posting the eng org chart update after this talk, we are creating a Platform Eng team to consolidate runtime and infra reliability. lena?
05:21 Lena Ortiz: yep the Platform Eng lead role is open, internal candidates encouraged. the idea is to shorten feedback loops between runtime and infra.
05:32 Audience: mm-hmm
05:38 Jane Park: culture note: we hit 150 employees this week, which is exciting and a little wild. please remember to follow the new onboarding checklist, it's on the docs site.
05:52 Maya Rao: onboarding checklist includes security training, SOC2 handling, and codebase orientation. we ran a pilot and reduced first-week confusion by about 40% (self-reporting).
06:05 Jane Park: ok we'll open it up for q and a, please use raise hand or drop in chat.
06:20 Audience Member (Engineering): can you elaborate on pricing impact for Dedicated autoscale? will it shift to commit model or stay burstable?
06:30 Samir Patel: pricing: committed capacity remains - autoscale adds a burst policy and per-burst unit price. goal is predictability plus a lower marginal price vs on-demand cloud. we'll publish a detailed pricing doc.
06:50 Audience Member (Sales): any concerns with channel partners for Private GA?
06:55 Maya Rao: partners are pre-briefed, we have training sessions next tuesday; channel docs will include deployment nuances and partner responsibilities.
07:10 Alex Chen: on security/compliance - SOC2 report updated, audit logs for Private customers are available, and we have RBAC improvements in the console to support enterprise teams.
07:28 Audience murmurs
07:35 Jane Park: any blockers we should know about? technical or go-to-market?
07:40 Lena Ortiz: one blocker is a perf regression we saw in a nightly build affecting a small model family; engineering is tracking and rollback is possible. not a major customer-facing outage but needs attention.
08:00 Samir Patel: on go-to-market, a couple of deals in procurement are slow due to legal clauses around data residency; Private GA should help but legal team will need to accelerate templates.
08:20 Jane Park: legal, please prioritize a template for EEA customers.
08:25 Audience: noted
08:30 Q&A rapid fire: several people ask about conference presence, with a few asking for booth time; marketing will coordinate.
08:50 Audience Member (Marketing): what's the message for conferences?
08:55 Jane Park: focus on "Production-first inference" - emphasize reliability, cost controls, and Private. leave benchmarks to collateral.
09:10 Samir Patel: a quick note on telemetry - we're improving per-route token-level cost reports; product will demo this in next week's leadership sync.
09:25 Jane Park: okay wrap up: huge thanks, small list of action items will be posted in the all-hands channel.
09:35 Jane Park: final quick motivational note - we're delivering enterprise grade inference while staying developer friendly; that's rare and valuable, keep pushing.
09:50 Meeting ended.

Notes: Transcript occasionally mislabels acronyms (e g KV cache sometimes written as K v cache), and filler words/presentational asides are present. Referenced artifacts: Q2 metrics deck (link to be shared), Private GA docs (to be published), Dedicated autoscale deep dive (calendar invite).

Recap / Next steps:
- Samir: circulate Q2 deck and sales play by Aug 15.
- Alex + Infra: schedule canary deep dive by Aug 19.
- Maya: publish Private GA docs and compliance checklist by Aug 20.
- People Ops: post hiring/referral details by Aug 14.
